SHIFT_MULT=2.0 was a GUESS shipped in the same commit as the probe-validated DOM_MARGIN=0.75 and described with the same confidence. From N=1000 onward the threshold sits ABOVE the across-splice distance, switching boundary detection OFF entirely: 14 boundaries for 3213 true switches (recall 0.01), assembler collapsed to 1 domain, unlearn deleted the whole store. The relative-margin rule was never actually tested — it was starved of input by the broken detector.
sweep_domains.sh set 8 knobs that self_organize.py reads nowhere (the D_MODEL_B failure mode). Running it would have produced meaningless duplicate rows that look like a clean null result.

DOM_RADIUS completely inert (0 of 143 domains ever learned a radius): a domain accumulates distance samples only when MATCHED, but matching requires a radius, and it bootstrapped from the broken NEW_DIST — a censored sample, the identical error already made once with the adaptive spawn threshold. A pooled prior was added and also failed (pool held 3-5 samples).

manage() NEVER RAN. Domain management shared MANAGE_EVERY=500 with the expert/world populations; a 468-step run never hits step%500==0 and the 937-step GH200 runs hit it exactly once. Merge, cull and the recurrence fold were off by arithmetic in EVERY domain number the project had reported, the 142-domain result included.
Background CPU tasks repeatedly killed around the 10-minute mark (exit codes 143/144) — cap-invariance test, unit grids, several tool calls timed out at 2m/6m40s/9m50s.

BATCH_W phase-lock — the largest instrumentation bug of the chunk. `assigns.append(...)`, the online-tokenizer block, CKPT_EVERY and the LM loss curve all sit BELOW `if len(_bx) < BATCH_W: i += WIN; step += 1; continue`, while `step` increments on every window. Flushes land on a fixed residue mod BATCH_W, so `step % N == 0` is unsolvable for EVERY BATCH_W>1. At Run A's BATCH_W=16: 6.2% of windows recorded, 0 mints, 0 retokenizations, 0 checkpoints (a multi-day run would never have saved).

The adaptive warmup printed 'stopped at N/N on separation plateau' when no plateau was detected. `_wfloor = min(ENC_WARMUP_MIN, wu)` with test `t >= _wfloor` over `range(wu)` means ENC_WARMUP_MIN == ENC_WARMUP makes the test unreachable — the single setting that disables the feature, and the user's runs used it, paying all 30,000 encoder steps.

The background workflow died when the container was reclaimed and restarted — not stalled. 2 of 5 diagnosis agents had returned; the verify phase never ran and no notification would ever arrive. Claude's earlier '~2 more hours, running at concurrency 2' diagnosis was wrong.

Two defects in the domain-genuineness report, both Claude's: (1) `sizes` was built from the subsampled `assigns`, so every size was ~16x understated in Run A and the size>=20 gate 16x too strict; (2) `separation` was a min over the other N-1 centroids, an extreme order statistic that shrinks mechanically as the population grows — it punished exactly the fragmentation the fold exists to reduce.

The COLLAPSE CHECK metric, shipped one commit earlier and never calibrated, printed 'signature space is COLLAPSED -- fix the ENCODER' at -5.2 sigma. A checkpoint with a measurably healthy encoder (true silhouette +0.25, 1-NN 0.90) scores -4.8 sigma. The null (random unit vectors in 64-d) was never right — centroids of related text are nowhere near orthogonal.

SigEncoder allocated nn.Embedding(V, d) with V=VMAX=16384 in online-tokenizer mode, but ENC_SEQ is always the raw BYTE stream there — only ids 0-255 reachable. ~77% of encoder params (12.4M) were dead weight touched by AdamW every step, plus 148 MB of optimizer state.

SAVE_CKPT=0 (Claude's own usage, meaning 'off') created a directory literally named `0` in the repo root — SAVE_CKPT is a PATH and "0" is truthy, so `if not ck: return` never fired. .gitignore covered *.pt and runs/ but not `0/` or `source.bin`, so `git add -A` committed 3.7 MB of checkpoint into the repo.

Two bugs introduced by the SIG_WIN/SIG_SPACE work: the lookahead window builder still hard-coded WIN as the byte width (ValueError: expected sequence of length 256, got 128), and contrastive_step was handed `bpos` (a byte offset) while ENC_SEQ had become the token stream (IndexError: index 36275 out of bounds).

Claude handed the user a GPU command containing a literal placeholder `... (same line otherwise)`, which failed as a bash error when the user ran it.
